name: Opus Quality Defensive
strategy: Long-only cross-asset carry and trend book, de-risked after energy trends broke: systematic managed-futures trend as the largest sleeve, a reduced commodity carry sleeve, a trimmed midstream sleeve, an enlarged equity variance-premium sleeve to harvest elevated implied vol, and 40% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: Research this week (web search plus Yahoo price pulls): crude had its worst week since 2020 on US-Iran peace bets after the Democratic midterm sweep. Brent fell from $117.64 to $98.32 and WTI from $104 to $90.83. XOP was stopped out at 174.10 on 11-05, and every remaining energy-linked carry leg is red: PDBC -6.85%, AMLP -5.78%. Two of my own rules now say de-risk. First, the energy trend broke: PDBC is below its 50-day average, and AMLP is below both its 50- and 100-day averages. Second, curve backwardation, the source of PDBC's roll carry, compresses as the war premium unwinds. I cut PDBC from 26% to 14% and AMLP from 12% to 8%. I do not exit either, because no deal is signed and Hormuz tanker attacks keep upside risk. DBMF stays at 22%: a systematic trend allocator re-weights itself, and it is only 3.7% under entry. JEPI rises from 11% to 16% because VIX jumped to 25-28 after the 11-05 4.4% S&P drop, which makes the covered-call premium richer. Gold stays closed because its trend is still down (about $4,075 against roughly $4,400 in August). Freed capital and the XOP proceeds sit in cash at 4%. This book shares no symbols with the Round 2 book (XLV/USMV/QUAL/XLE), so novelty overlap is 0%. All legs re-enter at the 11-09 close.

positions.thesis: A systematic managed-futures replication is the trend engine of the book and adapts to the energy and equity reversals without my discretion. It is only 3.7% below entry and near its 100-day average. Kept at 22% as the largest sleeve, since crisis-alpha behavior is what a VIX-25 tape needs.

This is the equity variance-premium sleeve. With VIX at 25 after spiking to 28, the index call premium JEPI sells is much richer, which raises its income carry, and its low-beta stock basket fell only 1.1% on the leg through a 4.4% S&P day. Raised from 11% to 16%.

This is the commodity backwardation carry sleeve. Its roll yield is shrinking as crude's war premium unwinds, and price is below the 50-day average, so it is cut from 26% to 14%. I keep some exposure because Brent at $98 is still well above pre-war levels, Hormuz attacks continue and no deal is signed. The stop is tightened to 10% from the new entry.

This is the midstream MLP carry sleeve. Fee-based pipeline cash flows and a high distribution yield are less tied to the crude price than E&P is, but AMLP has broken below its 50- and 100-day averages (50.24 against about 53.6), so the trend filter cuts it from 12% to 8%, with a 10% stop.
